_readme: Who each company is, for the Introduction tab: a short blurb, the parent's own site in China
(or global) and its US site where one exists, and a slot for a representative photo of one of
its outlets in China. LINKS ARE PROVIDED AS-IS. Any link outside the USA is untested by this
project and should be treated at the reader's discretion — the site warns of this beside every
such link. PHOTOS are not shipped: `photo` names a local file under map/img/ that must be an
image the project has the right to use (licensed, or an official press image with permission);
until one is added the tab shows a neutral placeholder. Never hotlink a copyrighted storefront
photo. `photo_credit` is shown beneath the image when present.

mixue.name: MIXUE
mixue.blurb: The world's largest fast-food chain by store count, with nearly 60,000 outlets. It runs on very low prices, such as an ice cream cone for under a dollar, and a franchise model that makes most of its money selling ingredients to franchisees. Its mascot is a crowned Snow King. US stores began opening in 2025.

us.label: New York, NY

chagee.name: CHAGEE
chagee.blurb: A fast-growing premium tea brand whose Chinese name is Bawang Chaji. It is often described as China's answer to Starbucks, and is known for its oolong-milk teas and plain branding. It listed on Nasdaq in 2025 and opened its first US stores the same year.

china.caption: A CHAGEE on Fotang Old Street, Yiwu, China
china.label: 义乌

gallery.caption: A CHAGEE counter in a mall

luckin.name: Luckin Coffee
luckin.blurb: China's largest coffee chain. It passed Starbucks in China by volume, using cheap, app-first ordering, and did so after rebuilding from a 2020 accounting fraud that had it delisted. It opened its first US stores in New York in mid-2025.

china.caption: A Luckin Coffee in Beijing, China
china.label: 北京

us.caption: A US Luckin Coffee (Sixth Avenue, Manhattan)
us.label: New York, NY

miniso.name: MINISO
miniso.blurb: A variety retailer selling inexpensive, design-focused goods and licensed-character merchandise. It has a Japanese-styled look but Guangzhou roots. Today, MINISO has the largest and most established US presence of any chain tracked here.

china.caption: A MINISO in Dongguan, China
china.label: 东莞

us.caption: A US MINISO in Times Square, New York
us.label: New York, NY

popmart.name: POP MART
popmart.blurb: The blind-box toy company behind Labubu and other collectible figures, sold through staffed stores and unstaffed “Robo Shop” vending kiosks. Its US presence has grown quickly in malls across the country.
popmart.first_outlet: East Rutherford, NJ — American Dream (first permanent store)

china.caption: A POP MART store in Beijing, China
china.label: 北京

us.caption: A US POP MART store (the Oculus, New York)
us.label: New York, NY

gallery.caption: A POP MART “roboshop” vending machine in Cerritos, California
A POP MART store in Suzhou, China

haidilao.name: Haidilao
haidilao.blurb: A large hot pot chain known for its elaborate service, which can include free manicures, live noodle-pulling and birthday songs. Its overseas arm, Super Hi International, runs the US restaurants, and it has been in the US since 2013.
haidilao.first_outlet: Arcadia, CA — 400 S Baldwin Ave (Westfield Santa Anita)

china.label: 苏州
china.caption: A Haidilao in Suzhou, China

gallery.caption: At a shopping-mall branch in China

heytea.name: HEYTEA
heytea.blurb: The brand that made cheese-foam and fresh-fruit tea popular in China, at the premium end of the market. Its US stores cluster in Chinese-American neighbourhoods. It publishes no US store locator, so we put its footprint together from public records.

china.caption: A HEYTEA in Zhengzhou, China
china.label: 郑州

gallery.caption: A HEYTEA store in Hong Kong

cotti.name: Cotti Coffee
cotti.blurb: Founded in 2022 by two executives who had been forced out of Luckin, and set up in direct competition with it. Cotti competes on price and has expanded worldwide very fast on a franchise model. Its US growth is quiet and led by franchisees, with no public US locator.
cotti.first_outlet: Pearl City, HI — Pearl Highlands Center

china.caption: A Cotti Coffee in Xiamen, China
china.label: 厦门

taier.name: Tai Er
taier.blurb: A Sichuan sauerkraut-fish (suancai yu) restaurant from the Hong Kong-listed group Jiumaojiu, known for its stylised branding and one signature dish. Its US presence is small and new, in San Mateo, San Jose, Flushing and LA.
taier.first_outlet: City of Industry, CA — 18518 E Gale Ave

china.caption: A Tai Er sauerkraut-fish restaurant in Zhengzhou, China
china.label: 郑州

gallery.caption: A Tai Er in Hong Kong

chabaidao.name: ChaPanda
chabaidao.blurb: A large Chinese fruit-tea chain (Chabaidao) that listed in Hong Kong in 2024. It entered the US in 2025 trading as “TeaByDo”, with only a handful of stores so far.

china.caption: A ChaPanda (Chabaidao) in Zhengzhou, China
china.label: 郑州

nayuki.name: NaiSnow
nayuki.blurb: The US arm of Nayuki (Naixue), a premium Hong Kong-listed tea-and-soft-bread chain, trading in America as “NaiSnow”. It entered the US in late 2025 and is expanding quickly across New York and into New Jersey.

china.caption: A Nayuki in Zhengzhou, China
china.label: 郑州

gallery.caption: A Nayuki Pro store in Suzhou

juewei.name: Juewei
juewei.blurb: A Shanghai-listed braised-snack chain (“duck neck” and other marinated items) with tens of thousands of outlets in China. Its US presence is tiny and mostly delivery, trading as Juewei Yabo, Jue Wei Kitchen and Jue Wei Food.

china.caption: A Juewei duck-neck shop in Beijing, China
china.label: 北京

gallery.caption: A Juewei counter in Changsha, China
A Juewei storefront in Changsha, China

yangguofu.name: Yangguofu
yangguofu.blurb: One of China's two dominant malatang (build-your-own skewered hotpot soup) chains, founded in Harbin in 2003. It began a registered US franchise programme in 2024, trading as YGF, and is expanding across the coasts.

fishwithyou.name: Fish With You
fishwithyou.blurb: A Chinese fast-casual chain built on one dish: Sichuan sauerkraut fish (suancai yu) over rice. Founded in Beijing around 2016, it has thousands of outlets in China. In the US it trades under several names (Fish With You, YONNY, Wei's Fish), using per-store sites rather than one locator.

yangs.name: Yang's Braised Chicken Rice
yangs.blurb: A braised-chicken-over-rice brand that was one of the earliest Chinese chains in America, trading since 2017, but is now in retreat, with most of its US restaurants closed. We include it because it is here, and because tracking a chain that opens and then quietly closes is part of the point of a daily count.

zhangliang.name: Zhang Liang Malatang
zhangliang.blurb: One of China's two dominant malatang (build-your-own skewered hotpot soup) chains, alongside Yangguofu, founded in Harbin in 2008 with around 6,000 outlets. Its self-serve format lets diners fill a bowl from 80-plus fresh ingredients cooked in a spicy bone broth. Its own brand news reports 42 North American outlets across the US, Canada and Mexico as of September 2026; in the US it clusters in California, in the Bay Area and Los Angeles.

china.caption: A Zhang Liang Malatang in Zhengzhou, China
china.label: 郑州

us.caption: A US Zhang Liang Malatang (Chinatown, Manhattan)
us.label: New York, NY

gallery.caption: Another US branch, in Flushing, Queens

chahalo.name: ChaHalo
chahalo.blurb: A premium "modern Chinese tea" chain founded in 2016 in Xi'an, known for tea-forward drinks made with whole tea leaves and fresh milk and a signature "tri-aroma" style. It has grown to around 1,000 stores across China and began expanding overseas in 2024; its early US outlets are in California and New York, with Canada (Toronto) also underway.

xiaolongkan.name: Shoo Loong Kan Hotpot
xiaolongkan.blurb: A Sichuan (mala) hotpot chain founded in Chengdu in 2014, one of China's largest with thousands of outlets, known for its numbing-spicy broth and old-Chengdu styling. It trades in the US as "Shoo Loong Kan Hotpot" and — unusually for the chains here — publishes its own US store locator.

gallery.caption: A Xiaolongkan (Shoo Loong Kan) hot pot in Madrid
A Shoo Loong Kan in Frankfurt

liuyishou.name: Liuyishou Hot Pot
liuyishou.blurb: A Chongqing hotpot chain founded in 2000, one of China's largest with thousands of outlets, known for its buttery mala broth and beef. It trades across North America as "Liuyishou Hot Pot" and publishes its own site with a page per city; its US outlets run from Boston and New York to California, Texas, Illinois and Washington.

aunteajenny.name: Auntea Jenny
aunteajenny.blurb: A bubble-tea chain founded in 2013 in Shanghai, one of China's largest with several thousand outlets and a 2025 Hong Kong listing, known for fresh-brewed milk teas and grain-based drinks. It entered the US as "Auntea Jenny", with its first outlets in New York and California and many more announced.

china.caption: An Auntea Jenny in Beijing, China
china.label: 北京

gallery.caption: An Auntea Jenny storefront in Beijing

mollytea.name: Molly Tea
mollytea.blurb: A Chinese premium milk-tea chain founded in 2021, known for its jasmine-tea "milk white" drinks and fast overseas growth across Asia, Australia and North America. Its US outlets, trading as "Molly Tea", run across California and into Washington, Texas, Illinois, Georgia, Nevada, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and beyond.
mollytea.first_outlet: Flushing, Queens, NY — 37-11 Prince St (since closed)

china.caption: A Molly Tea in Shenzhen, China
china.label: 深圳

gallery.caption: A Molly Tea store in Jakarta

lelecha.name: Lelecha
lelecha.blurb: A premium "modern Chinese tea" chain founded in 2016 in Shanghai, known for cheese-foam teas, fruit teas and its dirty-bun bakery. It has begun opening in the US, though its US site is not yet public; early outlets are in California.

china.caption: A Lelecha in Suzhou, China
china.label: 苏州

nonggengji.name: Nong Geng Ji
nonggengji.blurb: A Hunan-cuisine restaurant chain from Shenzhen known for countryside-style, wok-charred cooking with fresh peppers and family-style dishes. Its first US restaurant opened in Flushing, Queens in January 2026, with a second announced for Rockville, Maryland.

china.caption: A Nong Geng Ji Hunan restaurant in Beijing, China
china.label: 北京

gallery.caption: A Nong Geng Ji in Beijing

baospastry.name: Bao's Pastry
baospastry.blurb: A Beijing-headquartered bakery chain founded by Bao Caisheng about two decades ago, famous in China for its pork-floss cakes and cream-filled sponge, with more than 100 outlets. Its first US store opened in Flushing, Queens in late 2025.

china.caption: A Bao's Pastry in Suzhou, China
china.label: 苏州

gallery.caption: Queues at a Bao's Pastry in Beijing

toptoy.name: TOP TOY
toptoy.blurb: A Chinese art-toy and blind-box retailer launched in 2020 by MINISO Group, carrying its own IPs alongside licensed lines from Sanrio, Disney and others. It opened its first US store in Times Square, New York.

china.caption: A TOP TOY in Guangzhou, China
china.label: 广州

toys52.name: 52Toys
toys52.blurb: A Chinese designer-toy and blind-box brand founded in 2015 in Beijing, known for its Panda Roll and BEASTBOX lines and mecha model kits. Its US retail presence has begun in Georgia, alongside an online store.

dezhuang.name: De Zhuang Hot Pot
dezhuang.blurb: A Chongqing hot-pot restaurant and seasoning group founded in 1999 by Li Dejian, grown to some 900 restaurants across China. Known for numbing-spicy Chongqing broth. It reached the US around early 2025 with a full hot-pot restaurant in Manhattan's East Village and a smaller 'De Hotpot Mini' express store near Seattle.
dezhuang.first_outlet: New York — 37 St Marks Pl (East Village)

meizhoudongpo.name: Meizhou Dongpo
meizhoudongpo.blurb: A Sichuan-cuisine sit-down chain founded in Beijing in 1996 by Wang Gang and Liang Di and named for the poet Su Dongpo. With about 114 restaurants in China, it was one of the earliest Chinese chains to reach America, opening a Los Angeles flagship in 2013. Two California restaurants remain open after several LA-area closures.
meizhoudongpo.first_outlet: Los Angeles — 10250 Santa Monica Blvd (Century City)

china.caption: Inside a Meizhou Dongpo in Beijing, China
china.label: 北京

gallery.caption: Kung Pao chicken at Meizhou Dongpo

shudaxia.name: Shu Da Xia Hotpot
shudaxia.blurb: A Chengdu hot-pot chain founded in 2015, styled around wuxia (martial-arts) imagery, with 600-plus outlets. Since 2023 it has been owned by the Xiaolongkan hot-pot group. Its single US restaurant, near Boston University, has operated since May 2022.

xibei.name: Xibei
xibei.blurb: The flagship brand of the Xibei group, which grew from a 1988 snack shop in Inner Mongolia into some 370 restaurants serving Northwestern-China oat-noodle and mutton dishes. Its US expansion began in Los Angeles in December 2024 and now spans four Southern California outlets under three names — a flagship, a dumpling shop and fast-casual 'Eatery' noodle bars.
xibei.first_outlet: Los Angeles — 3300 W Sunset Blvd (Silver Lake)

china.caption: A Xibei Youmiancun in Zhengzhou, China
china.label: 郑州

gallery.caption: Proso-millet cold cake, a Xibei specialty
A Xibei at David Plaza, Zhengzhou

grandmashome.name: Grandma's Home
grandmashome.blurb: A Hangzhou-cuisine chain founded in 1998 by Wu Guoping, known for affordable home-style Jiangnan cooking across 200-plus directly-run restaurants in China. Its first and so far only US restaurant opened in Manhattan's Flatiron district in early 2024.

china.caption: A Grandma's Home in Zhengzhou, China
china.label: 郑州

gallery.caption: A Grandma's Home at Suzhou Center

xijiade.name: Dumpling Xi
xijiade.blurb: A Northeastern-China shrimp-dumpling chain founded in 2002 in Hegang, Heilongjiang by Gao Defu, with 800-plus directly-operated stores. It trades in America as 'Dumpling Xi', opening its first US store in Flushing, Queens in February 2025 and a second in the East Village that July.

china.caption: A Xijiade dumpling shop in Shenzhen, China
china.label: 深圳

malubianbian.name: Ma Lu Bian Bian
malubianbian.blurb: A Chengdu chain founded in 2015 in the 'chuan chuan' style — DIY skewers cooked in a shared spicy hot pot — done up like a nostalgic 1980s roadside stall. It claims over a thousand outlets globally. Its US footprint has churned heavily since the first store opened in San Gabriel in 2019; an Orlando restaurant is the clearest currently-open location.
malubianbian.first_outlet: San Gabriel, CA — 301 W Valley Blvd (now closed)

feidachu.name: Chef Fei
feidachu.blurb: A Hunan-cuisine chain built on one signature dish — stir-fried pork with chili peppers (辣椒炒肉) — founded by Fei Lianghui in Hengyang, Hunan and unified under the 费大厨 name in 2016, with roughly 200 directly-managed restaurants across China. Marketed in America as 'China's King of Stir-Fry', it opened its first US restaurant at Westfield UTC in San Diego in September 2026.
feidachu.first_outlet: San Diego — 4301 La Jolla Village Dr (Westfield UTC)

china.caption: A Chef Fei (Fei Da Chu) in Zhengzhou, China
china.label: 郑州

dalongyi.name: Da Long Yi Hot Pot
dalongyi.blurb: A Chengdu hot-pot chain founded in 2013 in the city's Yulin district, grown through franchising to a claimed 2,000-plus stores with outlets abroad. Known for numbing-spicy Sichuan broth. Its US outlets run as independent franchises; two — in Long Island City and Boston — are currently open after earlier California and Seattle stores closed.
dalongyi.first_outlet: San Gabriel, CA — 250 W Valley Blvd (now closed)

shuyi.name: Shuyi Grass Jelly & Tea
shuyi.blurb: A grass-jelly milk-tea chain founded in 2007 in Chengdu by Wang Bin, whose signature drinks pile a cup half-full with grass jelly and other toppings; one of China's largest tea chains, with several thousand stores. Its US shops, trading as 'Shuyi Grass Jelly & Tea', are franchise-run — three are open in Virginia and the Bay Area after the original San Mateo store closed.
shuyi.first_outlet: San Mateo, CA — 165 E 4th Ave (now closed)

china.caption: A Shuyi Shaoxiancao in Changsha, China
china.label: 长沙

anta.name: Anta
anta.blurb: China's largest sportswear company, founded in 1991 in Jinjiang, Fujian, and listed in Hong Kong. The Anta brand runs roughly 9,900 stores across China; its parent group also owns or controls FILA, Descente and Amer Sports (Arc'teryx, Salomon, Wilson), though those are not Chinese brands and are tracked separately. Anta opened its first US store — a company-operated flagship in Beverly Hills — in February 2026, with NBA players it sponsors at the launch, and is expanding across Southeast Asia.
anta.first_outlet: Beverly Hills, CA — 330 N Beverly Dr

china.caption: An Anta Sports store in Beijing, China
china.label: 北京

gallery.caption: An Anta Sports store in Suzhou

urbanrevivo.name: Urban Revivo
urbanrevivo.blurb: A Guangzhou fashion retailer founded in 2006 and often called China's answer to Zara, known for large, design-led stores. It runs more than 400 stores, mostly in China and Southeast Asia, and has since expanded to the UK and the US; its parent, Fashion Momentum Group, is privately held. Urban Revivo opened its first US store — a roughly 30,000-square-foot flagship in SoHo — in February 2025.

china.caption: An Urban Revivo in Zhengzhou, China
china.label: 郑州

jnby.name: JNBY
jnby.blurb: A Hangzhou designer-fashion house, listed in Hong Kong, that runs a family of in-house women's and lifestyle labels — JNBY, Croquis, less, jnby by JNBY and Pomme de terre — across roughly 2,100 stores, almost all in China. In the United States its stores trade as “AGoodFun”, run by a local licensee, with locations in San Francisco and Seattle; earlier stores in Bellevue and SoHo, New York have closed.
jnby.first_outlet: Seattle, WA — 600 Pine St (Pacific Place), as AGoodFun

meilleurmoment.name: Meilleur Moment
meilleurmoment.blurb: A minimalist womenswear label from Hangzhou's Eifini group (伊芙丽), a privately held fashion company founded in 2001 with more than 600 stores across its brands in China. Meilleur Moment opened its first US store — a boutique in SoHo — in May 2025.
meilleurmoment.first_outlet: SoHo, New York, NY — 257 Elizabeth St

moreyogurt.name: More Yogurt
moreyogurt.blurb: A Shanghai chain of yogurt-based drinks and smoothies — its signature is an avocado yogurt smoothie — that uses the English name “More Yogurt”. It operates in Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore, and opened its first US store in Tustin, California in 2026, with a second announced for Flushing, New York.
moreyogurt.first_outlet: Tustin, CA — 2471 Park Ave (The District at Tustin Legacy)

moge.name: Möge Tee
moge.blurb: A Chinese bubble-tea chain (愿茶) that trades in the US as “Möge Tee”. It has grown quickly across the US — roughly 70 stores in 18 states by late 2026, clustered in the Northeast, Florida, Texas and California — collected daily from its own US store locator. (A different brand from Molly Tea / 茉莉奶白, and from More Yogurt / 茉酸奶.)

juqi.name: JUQI
juqi.blurb: A Beijing home-style restaurant chain (~20 outlets in China) known for playful old-Beijing dishes — Lord-Rabbit mashed potato, honeycomb-briquette fried rice and Peking duck. Its first US location opened at the Tangram complex in Flushing, Queens.
juqi.us_since_note: Flushing (Tangram) announced Oct 2019 for a 2020 opening (Patch); still a single US store — long-standing (exact year 2020-2022 uncertain).

leebai.name: Lee & Bai
leebai.blurb: A Chengdu buns-and-noodles chain (李与白包子铺) with hundreds of outlets in China, known for fresh-steamed baozi, Chengdu pickled-pork bao and zapu noodles. It is expanding across the US, with outlets in New York, California and New Jersey.

quanjude.name: Quanjude
quanjude.blurb: The Beijing roast-duck institution (全聚德), founded 1864, whose hanging-oven Peking duck method is a National Intangible Cultural Heritage. A state-owned chain with 100+ outlets in China; its US flagship opened in Midtown Manhattan under the upscale 'iDEN' concept (iDEN & Quanjude).
quanjude.first_outlet: New York, NY — 3 E 52nd St (iDEN & Quanjude)

china.caption: Quanjude's original roast-duck restaurant in Beijing, China
china.label: 北京

gallery.caption: A chef carving Beijing roast duck at Quanjude

mamaxita.name: Mama Xita BBQ
mamaxita.blurb: A Chinese-Korean-style barbecue chain from the Xita Korean-BBQ district of Shenyang (Liaoning), with 450+ outlets across 31 Asian cities, run by the Chubby Group (which also operates Chubby Cattle). Its first US location opened in Bellevue, Washington.

gallery.caption: A Mama Xita BBQ dining room
A dish at Mama Xita BBQ

shanchenglameizi.name: Shancheng Lameizi
shanchenglameizi.blurb: A Chongqing hot-pot brand (山城辣妹子, 'Chongqing spicy girl') known for fiery beef-tallow broths and hand-cut fresh beef and tripe. China-origin (with a Beijing outlet); its US outlets operate under one Southern California group. Menu/pricing at shanchenglameizi.com (and its online-ordering pages) — kept for a later Pro pricing catalog.

bingxue.name: BINGXUE
bingxue.blurb: A mass-market tea-and-ice-cream chain from Tai'an, Shandong (冰雪时光, founded 2014) — the budget, bear-mascot (“Bobo Bear”) rival to Mixue, selling fresh-fruit and milk teas, soft serve (it claims the world's best-selling matcha soft serve), yogurt smoothies and coffee. The brand reports about 5,000 stores across 18 countries, over 1,500 of them outside its home market. It opened its first US and North American store in downtown Davis, California on 2 October 2026 — a mayor-attended grand opening — with a second US store in development on Oxnard Boulevard.

china.caption: A Bingxue in Fuyuan, China
china.label: 抚远

walaida.name: WALAIDA
walaida.blurb: A Hunan-cuisine restaurant chain built on charcoal and dry-pot bullfrog (牛蛙), founded around 2009–2010 in Changsha, Hunan by siblings Luo Hao and Luo Qing and later headquartered in Shenzhen. It has grown to roughly 460–500 outlets across more than 90 Chinese cities, about 90% of them franchised. Its first tracked US outlet operates in Flushing, New York, as 蛙来哒法拉盛店 (WALAIDA Flushing).
walaida.us_since_note: Operating Oct 2026 (Google, Flushing, ~140 reviews); exact opening date not established.

jibeichuan.name: JiBeiChuan
jibeichuan.blurb: A rice-noodle chain built on fish-maw chicken-soup rice noodles (花胶鸡汤米粉), prepared in 2018 with its first direct-operated store in 2019 and headquartered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang (Hangzhou Shengli Catering Management Co.). It runs direct-operated and partner stores across China (Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Hunan, Hubei, Henan) and in North America (the US and Canada). Its US outlets include three in New York City — Flushing, Manhattan and Brooklyn — and one in San Leandro, California.

babakehouse.name: BA Artisan Bakehouse
babakehouse.blurb: A French-Asian artisan bakery chain founded in 2016 in Kunming, Yunnan — 'BA' is short for BON APPÉTIT (French for 'enjoy your meal'), operated by Yunnan Bangnaboudi Food Development Co. (邦纳博地). It has grown to about 45 stores across China (Kunming, Chongqing, Xi'an, Chengdu and more), with overseas stores in Dubai and the US. Its North America flagship opened in Bellevue, Washington in January 2026.

chicjoc.name: CHICJOC
chicjoc.blurb: A Shanghai "minimalist-luxury" (极简极奢) womenswear brand operated by Shanghai Jiuci Brand Management Co. (上海玖赐), founded 2015. It began as a Taobao online brand and moved offline in May 2022 (first store at Nanjing Deji Plaza), growing to roughly 40–50 brick-and-mortar stores across first- and key second-tier Chinese cities' high-end malls, backed by four own factories. Its first overseas store opened at the Beverly Center in Los Angeles in November 2024; it also trades at Fashion Island in Newport Beach and in Paris.
chicjoc.first_outlet: Los Angeles, CA — Beverly Center, 8500 Beverly Blvd

dreame.name: DREAME
dreame.blurb: A Suzhou (Jiangsu) smart-home electronics brand (Dreame Technology, 追觅科技; Xiaomi-ecosystem origin) known for robot vacuums, cordless stick vacuums, wet/dry cleaners and hair dryers. In the US it runs a growing branded retail chain of smart-home stores — a chain rather than a single flagship — with permanent locations at Westfield Century City (Los Angeles), Westfield UTC (San Diego), Westfield Valley Fair (Santa Clara) and Garden State Plaza (Paramus, NJ), alongside temporary pop-ups.
dreame.first_outlet: Los Angeles, CA — Westfield Century City

showminihotpot.name: Show Mini Hot Pot
showminihotpot.blurb: A golden-soup malatang chain (金汤麻辣烫, branded 'mini hot pot' in the US — customizable, individual-serving malatang) operated by Harbin Yuxiangding Catering Management Co. (哈尔滨裕祥鼎), founded 2016 in Harbin, Heilongjiang. By mid-2025 it had about 693 stores across China (Heilongjiang, Anhui, Jilin, Hebei), run on a franchise model with a central kitchen. It entered the US in 2025; its Richardson, Texas store (CityLine) is operating, and it has announced several more US cities as coming soon.

rolife.name: Rolife
rolife.blurb: An IP-toy and lifestyle-creative brand of Robotime Group (若态科技, Suzhou, founded 2007; the Rolife sub-brand launched 2017), known for DIY miniature dollhouses, 3D wooden puzzles and IP art toys — its headline character Nanci is sold as blind boxes. In the US it runs a growing branded retail chain of about a dozen stores across seven states; it also operates stores in China, Thailand, Japan and the Netherlands.

nanhotpot.name: Nan Hotpot
nanhotpot.blurb: A Chongqing-style hotpot chain (楠火锅) founded in 1993, headquartered in Chengdu under Chengdu Shangzong Group (成都上纵集团), known for a heavy beef-tallow base and a 'market-stall / old-alley' (巷子里的老火锅) store concept. It has grown to 590–600+ stores and expanded abroad through a North America division with signed cooperative/franchise partners. Its overseas-first store opened in the Seattle area (Bellevue, WA) in March 2023, and it also trades in Plano, Texas.

huaxiaoxiao.name: Hwa ShooShoo
huaxiaoxiao.blurb: A Xinjiang fried-rice-noodle (新疆炒米粉) fast-casual chain founded in 2019–2020, with its first store in Beijing (Wangjing) and incubated/operated by 四有青年餐创集团 (Beijing Siyou Qingnian, est. 2015) under the slogan 让世界爱上新疆味 ('let the world fall in love with the taste of Xinjiang'). It grew to roughly 3,500 stores by the end of 2025 and 4,000+ by mid-2026. Its overseas-first store opened in Flushing, New York (Tangram food court) in February 2025 — billed as the first Xinjiang fried-rice-noodle brand to reach North America.
huaxiaoxiao.first_outlet: Flushing, NY — Tangram food court (overseas-first store)

zhoumapo.name: Zhoumapo
zhoumapo.blurb: A fast-casual Sichuan stir-fry (快餐式小炒) chain founded in August 2012 by Zhou Hongxia (周红霞), with its parent 福建省周麻婆餐饮管理有限公司 (Fujian Zhou Mapo Catering Management) headquartered in Fuzhou, Fujian. Known for a ¥2 Mapo tofu and 'tasty, fast, affordable' positioning, it grew to roughly 300 franchised stores by 2021. Its first US store opened at 728 Eighth Avenue in Times Square, New York (a 10-year lease signed in January 2025), trading as 'Mapo Asian Restaurant & Bar — Time Square 周麻婆' — repositioned as a full restaurant and bar while keeping the Mrs. Zhou brand and grandma logo.
zhoumapo.first_outlet: New York, NY — Times Square (728 8th Ave)

littlesheep.name: Little Sheep Hot Pot
littlesheep.blurb: A Mongolian hot-pot chain founded 1999 in Baotou, Inner Mongolia and owned by Yum China since 2012 — not to be confused with Happy Lamb (快乐小羊), the separate brand its founder re-created in 2017. After its earlier US outlets were largely renamed Happy Lamb, Little Sheep re-entered the US in 2026 with a new location at American Dream, New Jersey.
littlesheep.first_outlet: East Rutherford, NJ — American Dream (US re-entry)

yaoyao.name: YAOYAO
yaoyao.blurb: YAOYAO (姚姚酸菜鱼) is a China-origin Sichuan pickled-fish (酸菜鱼) chain founded in Shenzhen in 2016 by Yao Minxi, a former Huawei executive. Known for its Tiffany-blue 'light-luxury' interiors and bear-fish mascot, it grew to roughly 50-70 stores and has repeatedly ranked among China's top pickled-fish brands. In the US it operates three outlets — Chicago's Chinatown (a Michelin Bib Gourmand pick in 2024 and 2025), San Leandro, and San Bruno, California (the last co-branded 'Jin Gege & Yao Yao'). It opened and then fully withdrew from Hong Kong, where all four of its stores have closed.

bingz.name: Bingz
bingz.us_since_note: Grand opening 2 Oct 2026 (San Gabriel, TAWA Gateway).
bingz.first_outlet: San Gabriel, CA — 140 W Valley Blvd Ste 118C

dusu.name: Dusu Bakery
dusu.us_since_note: Opened by Sep 2026 (The Infatuation LA, 30 Sep 2026, 'has opened'); exact month not established.

hibake.name: Hi Bake
hibake.us_since_note: First overseas store Aug 2025 (Beverly Hills), per Chinese trade press.
hibake.first_outlet: Beverly Hills, CA — 235 N Canon Dr

yogost.name: Hey! I am Yogost
yogost.blurb: Hey! I am Yogost (我是酸奶君) is a China-origin yogurt-drink chain founded in Shenzhen in 2017, operated by Shenzhen Baichengduoyi Restaurant Management Co. It is known for purple-rice yogurt drinks and a cute bear-chef mascot, with roughly 70-plus stores across China, Hong Kong, Australia, New Zealand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Canada and the United States. Its North American footprint, per the brand's own store locator, spans 12 Canadian outlets (Alberta, British Columbia, Ontario, Manitoba and Saskatchewan) and three US stores: Philadelphia, Boston and American Dream in New Jersey (the last opened in 2026).
yogost.first_outlet: Philadelphia, PA / Boston, MA / East Rutherford, NJ (American Dream)

ximivogue.name: XIMIVOGUE
ximivogue.blurb: XIMIVOGUE is a China-origin variety and lifestyle retailer founded in 2015 and headquartered in Guangzhou. Like Miniso, it markets a Korean/Japanese design aesthetic despite being a Chinese company, selling an inexpensive, wide range of household goods, beauty products, accessories and toys. It has grown to well over a thousand stores across 90-plus countries through franchising, including US locations in Georgia, Illinois and Florida.
ximivogue.first_outlet: Lawrenceville GA / Schaumburg IL / Orlando FL / Miami FL

derucci.name: DeRUCCI
derucci.blurb: DeRUCCI (慕思) is a China-origin premium mattress, bedding and furniture company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Dongguan, Guangdong; its parent, DeRUCCI Health Sleep Co., listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2022. Like Miniso, it wraps a European-designer image around what is a Chinese company, and operates roughly four thousand stores in China out of a global footprint above five thousand. It entered the US market with showrooms in New York, California and Georgia.
derucci.first_outlet: Arcadia CA (Santa Anita) / Flushing NY (Sky View)

mogouyan.name: Mogouyan Hand-Pulled Noodle
mogouyan.blurb: Mogouyan Hand-Pulled Noodle is a China-origin Lanzhou-style beef-noodle chain named after the Mogouyan district of Lanzhou, Gansu, where it traces 40-50 years of history. It expanded abroad starting with Toronto in 2019 and is concentrated in Canada; its first US location opened at Mall of America in Bloomington, Minnesota, featuring live hand-pulling of its noodles.

rbtea.name: R&B Tea
rbtea.blurb: R&B Tea is a bubble-tea chain named for the initials of its founders, Rex and Bruce. Founder Bruce is Taiwanese but launched the brand while working in Suzhou, China: the first R&B Tea store opened in Suzhou in 2006, and the chain was built out across China — a reported 1,000-plus shops worldwide — before expanding to Singapore, Macau, Malaysia and Indonesia. Its US arm, R&B Tea USA (HQ Gardena/Garden Grove, California), operates 40 stores across California, Texas, Arizona, Michigan, South Carolina and North Carolina. It is tracked as China-born-and-built, distinct from the Taiwan-HQ tea chains the project excludes.

tenseconds.name: Ten Seconds Yunnan Rice Noodle
tenseconds.blurb: Ten Seconds Yunnan Rice Noodle (十秒到云南过桥米线, ShiMiaoDao) is a China-origin chain built around Yunnan "crossing-the-bridge" rice noodles, headquartered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang. After scaling across China it expanded overseas — its own history dates its first overseas store to New York — and now reports 40-plus North America locations. Operator-observed Google Maps listings confirm about 44 operating US stores across 19 states, concentrated in California and Texas, with its signature noodles served in a steaming stone pot.

caoshiyabo.name: Caoshiyabo
caoshiyabo.blurb: China-origin braised duck-neck (卤味) snack brand traced to a ~2003 street cart (Changsha, Hunan / Chengdu); ~2,000+ franchised stores across 300+ Chinese cities. The name is CONTESTED — multiple separate China companies (成都团结曹氏, 成都蜀湘曹氏, 湖南曹氏鸭脖) operate under it amid trademark disputes, so no single corporate owner is asserted here. Present in Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, Johor); the local 'Caoshiyabo Malaysia' operation's exact China parent / authorization is unconfirmed. No US presence.

ningji.name: Ningji Lemon Tea
ningji.blurb: 3,000+ hand-smashed-lemon-tea (手打柠檬茶) stores; founded 2021 in Changsha, Hunan (founder Wang Jie; Tencent/ByteDance/Shunwei-backed). Overseas since 2025 — open in Malaysia, Singapore and Cambodia, with Australia and New Zealand signed. Its US entry, branded 'Bobobaba' (Glendale, CA), opened in April 2026 and closed within months.

ningqi.name: NingQi
ningqi.blurb: Yunnan glutinous-rice-scented tea brand (糯米香叶 / 东方香茶); founded October 2021 in Yunnan (founder Huang Lei). 200+ stores across 30+ Chinese cities within a year; overseas debut in Malaysia (Sutera Mall, Johor Bahru). No US presence.

yihetang.name: Yihetang
yihetang.blurb: 8,000+ contracted stores (Dec 2024), overwhelmingly China; ~60 international stores in a Vietnam-Thailand-Malaysia-Indonesia SE-Asia cluster (early 2026)

tianlala.name: Tianlala
tianlala.blurb: ~8,000 China stores + 200+ overseas (Feb 2025); trademarks in 52 countries; overseas ops HQ Singapore (2023), SE Asia + Central Asia focus

luckycup.name: Lucky Cup
luckycup.blurb: Mixue's budget coffee arm; hit 10,000 stores (Nov 2025), almost all in China; overseas brand-new

yujianxiaomian.name: Yu Jian Xiao Mian
yujianxiaomian.blurb: ~500+ stores worldwide (Chongqing noodles, HKEX-listed Dec 2025); overseas since Dec 2025 and scaling in Hong Kong (19 stores by Oct 2026) plus 4 in Singapore

happylamb.name: Happy Lamb Hot Pot
happylamb.blurb: ~100+ Inner-Mongolian-style hot pot restaurants across ~11 countries. Re-founded 2017 by Zhang Gang (张钢), the founder of Little Sheep (小肥羊), after Yum! Brands acquired Little Sheep; first store Baotou (Inner Mongolia) Dec 2017, then Hohhot and Shijiazhuang. North American operations are run from a Houston, TX base.

teapulse.name: Teapulse
teapulse.blurb: 悸动烧仙草 (Jidong), a Shanghai new-tea / grass-jelly (烧仙草) chain ~19 years old with 2,000+ locations; began expanding abroad in 2019 (UK, Japan, Philippines, Laos, South Korea). Trades in the US as 'Teapulse' (first store Flushing NY ~2022, then a Manhattan expansion through 2026) and abroad as 'Jidong' / 'Jidong Herbal Jelly'.

hefu.name: Hefu Noodle
hefu.blurb: 632 stores (2025) across 80+ Chinese cities; overseas began in Hong Kong Feb 2024

xiabu.name: Xiabu Xiabu
xiabu.blurb: ~1,000+ outlets across the Xiabu + Coucou brands, overwhelmingly in China; the Xiabu brand's footprint outside China is ~21 across HK/Taiwan/Macau/Singapore (Jun 2024)

coucou.name: Coucou
coucou.blurb: Xiabu Xiabu's premium sub-brand (2016); ~200 branches mostly in China + Hong Kong; outside China in Hong Kong and Singapore

laowang.name: Laowang
laowang.blurb: China's largest pork-tripe-chicken (猪肚鸡) hotpot chain, ~135-150 restaurants in China; its only confirmed store outside China is one in Taipei

peijie.name: Peijie
peijie.blurb: Chongqing hotpot, ~30 mostly directly-operated stores in China; first overseas store Amsterdam (Oct 2025)

zhouheiya.name: Zhou Hei Ya
zhouheiya.blurb: ~1,000+ braised-duck snack stores, almost all in China (HK-listed 1458.HK — a stock listing only); a single overseas store

kkv.name: KKV
kkv.blurb: KK Group's lead overseas retail brand; the group has >1,000 China stores + 170+ overseas across 6 SE-Asian countries (Jun 2026)

x11.name: X11
x11.blurb: KK Group art-toy/trend retail brand (~64 stores Jan 2024, mostly China); a later overseas entrant, part of the group's 170+ overseas

colorist.name: The Colorist
colorist.blurb: KK Group cosmetics retail brand (2019); part of the group's 170+ overseas stores

cooltoy.name: Cool Toy
cooltoy.blurb: Ningbo art-toy retailer (~300 stores in 60+ Chinese cities); overseas nascent, retrenching domestically

muwu.name: Muwu BBQ
muwu.blurb: ~400+ directly-operated skewer/BBQ stores across ~20 Chinese cities; overseas early-stage (Hong Kong)

steelpipe.name: Steel Pipe No.5
steelpipe.name_zh: 钢管厂五区小郡肝串串香
steelpipe.blurb: ~880 skewer-hotpot (串串香) stores (Nov 2025), overwhelmingly in China; overseas is franchise-driven and name-fragmented, so attributions are brand-name-level, not corporate-confirmed

micun.name: Micun
micun.blurb: 1,900+ Korean-style bibimbap fast-food stores, nearly all in China; overseas footprint = Singapore only

greentea.name: Green Tea
greentea.blurb: China-origin 'New Zhejiang Cuisine' (新浙江菜) casual-dining chain — founded in Hangzhou, Zhejiang by chairman Wang Qinsong 王勤松 (group marked its 20th anniversary in 2024); ~500-700 stores, overwhelmingly in China; HKEX-listed 2025 (6831). Overseas expansion began 31 Aug 2024 with Hong Kong (Hysan Place), then The Wai Mall (Nov 2024) and SE Asia. Signature Zhejiang dishes (West Lake water-shield & fish-ball soup, Dongpo braised beef); bamboo-themed 'Jiangnan' interiors.

tanyu.name: Tanyu
tanyu.blurb: China-origin grilled-fish (烤魚) chain — founded Shenzhen 2013 (parent Gantang Mingshan 甘棠明善, Shenzhen); signature fresh-green-pepper grilled fish. 400+ stores across 80+ China cities; overseas across ~8 markets incl. Singapore (first flagship 2017), Malaysia (KL 2023) and Hong Kong. An earlier note cited North American outlets (a Flushing NY store and Vancouver), but a Tanyu is NOT currently observed in Flushing (Oct 2026) — US/Canada presence unconfirmed.

nanjingimpressions.name: Nanjing Impressions
nanjingimpressions.blurb: ~35-40 Nanjing-cuisine stores, all in China except a single overseas outlet

nowwa.name: Nowwa Coffee
nowwa.blurb: ~10,000 stores (Dec 2025) across 300+ cities, grown largely through Meiyijia convenience-store counters; overseas since 2024 — Macau, then its first standalone overseas store in Melbourne (Apr 2025) and Indonesia (Jan 2026), with more of Southeast Asia signed. North America is a stated expansion target in the company's own materials (and secondary coverage), but with no US city, franchise partner or date yet — watchlist, not announced.

manner.name: Manner Coffee
manner.blurb: Premium 'street coffee' chain founded 2015 in Shanghai, ~1,000 stores in China; making its first move outside China with a Hong Kong store (announced 2026, signage 'Maners Coffee').

yuanji.name: Yuanji Chuanchuanxiang
yuanji.blurb: Chengdu skewer-hotpot chain (founded 1996; distinct from the 袁记云饺 dumpling brand); claims industry-first overseas direct stores from 2016 in Canada, then the Netherlands and Australia.

xiaogujiejie.name: Xiaogujiejie
xiaogujiejie.blurb: Tianjin malatang chain (founded 2018), 1,000+ stores by Aug 2026. Company and trade press describe overseas stores across Japan, France, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Australia, Singapore and the US, but few are independently confirmed.

banu.name: Banu Maodu Hotpot
banu.blurb: Premium Henan hotpot chain (founded 2001, Anyang; ~240 directly-operated stores per banu.cn, Oct 2026). Going global with its first overseas store — Hysan Place, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, opening mid-November 2026, with a stated plan for 15–20 Hong Kong stores.

laoxiangji.name: Laoxiangji
laoxiangji.blurb: Hefei home-style chicken chain; opened its first overseas store in 2026 (Malaysia). Trades overseas as Lausanjee (Malaysia open; Singapore JV with Jumbo Group, 2026).

manling.name: Manling Congee
manling.blurb: Shanghai congee chain; overseas debut 2025 in Malaysia, then Spain.

xiaocaiyuan.name: Xiao Cai Yuan
xiaocaiyuan.blurb: Anhui home-style (徽菜) chain, HK-listed (HKEX 0999); announced Hong Kong as its overseas debut.

linlee.name: LINLEE
linlee.blurb: Foshan (Guangdong) tea brand; overseas expansion began with Hong Kong.

mstand.name: M Stand
mstand.blurb: Shanghai specialty-coffee chain (founded 2017); first overseas store in Japan.

meiyijia.name: Meiyijia
meiyijia.blurb: Dongguan convenience-store chain; expanding into Southeast Asia, partly under an 'Ohmee' brand.

crvanguard.name: CR Vanguard
crvanguard.blurb: China Resources supermarket group; long-established in Hong Kong.

qiandama.name: Qiandama
qiandama.blurb: Dongguan fresh-food/grocery chain; 72 stores across Hong Kong and Macau (2025), branded QDAMA.

bestore.name: Bestore
bestore.blurb: Wuhan packaged-snack retailer; first branded overseas flagship in Malaysia.

mglife.name: M&G LIFE
mglife.blurb: M&G/Chenguang lifestyle-stationery retailer (Jiumu Sundry Social); expanding in Southeast Asia.

bosideng.name: Bosideng
bosideng.blurb: Changshu down-jacket maker; a London flagship (reopened Oct 2022). European sales are otherwise wholesale.

semir.name: Semir
semir.blurb: Wenzhou mass-apparel group (森马服饰): Semir adult casual + Balabala 巴拉巴拉 kidswear (China's largest kidswear brand). 100+ overseas stores across ~15 markets — overseas/HK retail runs overwhelmingly under the Balabala banner.

xtep.name: Xtep
xtep.blurb: Quanzhou sportswear/running brand; mono-brand 'retail+community' stores in Malaysia and Singapore.

laopu.name: Laopu Gold
laopu.blurb: Beijing heritage-gold jeweller; Hong Kong and Macau, plus a first true overseas store in Singapore (Jun 2025).

lining.name: Li-Ning
lining.blurb: Beijing sportswear brand; a Hong Kong flagship (2022) and Southeast-Asia plans. An earlier US store (Portland) has closed.

moco.name: MO&Co.
moco.blurb: Guangzhou contemporary womenswear; standalone stores in Paris, London and Malaysia.

icicle.name: Icicle
icicle.blurb: Shanghai premium apparel house (owns France's Carven); boutiques in Paris incl. a 35 Av. George V flagship.

cabbeen.name: Cabbeen
cabbeen.blurb: Foshan designer menswear; first overseas stores in Malaysia, with more planned.

florasis.name: Florasis
florasis.blurb: Hangzhou heritage-cosmetics brand; a Tokyo flagship (Jan 2025) and a Paris counter (2024). US reach is retail shelves only.

maogeping.name: Mao Geping
maogeping.blurb: Prestige-makeup house (first HK-listed C-beauty, 1318); a department-counter model with a first overseas store in Hong Kong (2025).

judydoll.name: Judydoll
judydoll.blurb: Shanghai color cosmetics brand (Joy Group); standalone stores in Singapore and Hong Kong.

joocyee.name: Joocyee
joocyee.blurb: Shanghai color cosmetics brand (Joy Group, sister to Judydoll); first international store in Singapore.

xiaomi.name: Xiaomi
xiaomi.blurb: Consumer-electronics giant; 100+ own/franchised Mi Stores across Europe (incl. Poland), plus India, SE Asia and the Middle East. No US retail.

huawei.name: Huawei
huawei.blurb: Consumer-electronics maker; branded 'experience stores' across Europe (Madrid, Milan, Barcelona, Paris, Vienna). No US presence.

hotmaxx.name: HotMaxx
hotmaxx.blurb: Shanghai soft-discount / near-expiry snack & packaged-goods retailer (~950 stores); a Hong Kong store (Sep 2024), Japan announced.

makkee.name: Makkee Dessert
makkee.blurb: 麦记牛奶 (Mak Kee Milk Company), a Chinese dessert-soup (糖水/炖奶) chain founded 2021 in Huzhou, Zhejiang (founder Xu Kang) — milk-based takes on traditional Chinese tong sui. China's largest Chinese-dessert-soup chain by store count, ~1,000 outlets (up from ~53 at the start of 2025). Began expanding abroad in 2025: the United States (CA/NY/WA, trading as 'Makkee Dessert') and Australia (Sydney). Despite the Cantonese-style 'Mak Kee' branding it is Zhejiang-born, not Hong Kong.

guoquan.name: Guoquan
guoquan.blurb: Chinese home-dining-ingredients retailer (锅圈食汇 / GQ Homepot; HKEX 2517, listed Nov 2023) — hot pot and BBQ ingredient packs, ready-to-cook and ready-to-eat meals; more than 11,500 stores in China at the end of 2025. Opened its first store outside its home market on 19 Aug 2026, a Wan Chai flagship in Hong Kong with in-store dining, and set up its international regional HQ there as the launchpad for Southeast Asia, Europe and North America.

commune.name: COMMUNE
commune.blurb: Chinese restaurant-bar ('dining bar') chain (COMMUNE / 幻师), founded 2016 in Wuhan, HQ Zhuhai, Guangdong (Jiwu Siwei / Zhuhai Tangqi Shengtao) — a 'super bar + self-serve drinks + dining' format; ~112 directly-operated stores across 40 Chinese cities (Sep 2025). Opened its first store outside its home market on 24 Jul 2026, a Causeway Bay flagship (Lee Garden 3) in Hong Kong, branded COMMUNE MAISON.

shikao.name: Shikao Grilled Fish
shikao.blurb: Guangzhou-origin Chongqing-style tofu-flower grilled-fish chain (师烤豆花烤鱼; founded ~2019, 170-200+ outlets in China, a top grilled-fish brand, franchise program). Overseas: Singapore (Marine Parade), Canada (Ottawa + Mississauga), and Australia (Sydney Chinatown — a combined 'Shikao × Panda Hotpot 熊猫冲浪火锅' venue). Not yet in the US.

sanjin.name: Sanjin Tangbao
sanjin.blurb: Soup-dumpling (湯包) and pan-fried-bun QSR chain; brand created in Shenzhen 2014 (operator 深圳三津餐饮管理) by three founders from Huaining, Anhui — 5,300+ franchised stores (May 2023) across Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian, Jiangxi and Guangxi; a '国民早餐' (national breakfast) brand. Entered Hong Kong 20 Sept 2023 (Maxgrand Plaza, San Po Kong) — reportedly the first China soup-dumpling brand in HK; ~3 company-operated HK stores with HK-customised flavours. No known US presence.

baheli.name: Baheli
baheli.blurb: Chaoshan (潮汕)-style fresh-beef hotpot chain from Shantou, Guangdong; 200+ stores in China. Entered Hong Kong late 2024 — first store trial at New Town Plaza, Sha Tin (Nov 2024; officially opened 5 Dec 2024 per Invest HK), operated by 香港八合里餐飲管理. Planned 2-3 HK stores short-term, but that expansion is as-yet-unrealized; ~1 store (V Walk, Sham Shui Po) confirmed open Oct 2026. No known US presence.

chenpengpeng.name: Teochew Bistro
chenpengpeng.blurb: Shenzhen-based Chaoshan (潮汕/Teochew) cuisine chain, signature Chaoshan braised goose (卤鹅); grew from a braised-goose restaurant (陈鹏鹏卤鹅饭店, ~2016) into 陈鹏鹏潮汕菜 (~2021) — ~30-34 stores concentrated in Shenzhen/Guangdong. Entered Hong Kong: 1 store at New Town Plaza, Sha Tin (branded 'Teochew Bistro' / 陳鵬鵬潮汕菜). No known US presence.

gulugulu.name: GuluGulu
gulugulu.blurb: China-origin takoyaki (章魚燒/丸子) and milk-tea snack chain; reportedly founded in Guangzhou in 1997 (a Philippines franchisee cites 600+ China stores — unverified), with China stores (e.g. Shenzhen) and overseas branches (Singapore, Australia, Philippines). Entered Hong Kong — one store at Yau Ma Tei. No known US presence. (Origin/scale to re-verify.)

luobo.name: Luobo Xiangnan
luobo.blurb: China (Xiangxi / western Hunan)-style fast-food brand — hot-plate fried rice (鐵板炒飯) and Xiangxi pickles. Entered Hong Kong with one store at Dundas Square, Mong Kok (leased Dec 2023, opened Feb 2024) but CLOSED after ~4 months (~June 2024) amid 'poor local fit'. China chain scale UNCONFIRMED — possibly a limited/single venture. No known US presence.

tosummer.name: To Summer
tosummer.blurb: China-origin niche fragrance / home-scent brand — founded Beijing 2018 (劉惠璞 + 沈黎), 'new Chinese' (新中式) oriental perfumery, L'Oréal-backed; ~10+ China stores incl. Shanghai (湖南路 flagship), Beijing (國子監四合院), Wuxi and Nanjing. Hong Kong first overseas store at Causeway Bay. No known US presence.

hla.name: HLA
hla.blurb: China-origin menswear chain — founded Jiangyin, Jiangsu (周建平, 1988; brand launched ~2002), listed in Shanghai (600398); one of China's largest apparel chains (5,000+ stores). Overseas push includes Singapore (Suntec City, 2018). Signed its first Hong Kong lease in Central. No known US presence.

laomatou.name: Lao Ma Tou Hot Pot
laomatou.blurb: China-origin Sichuan hotpot chain (Chengdu; known for a clear 'no-sediment' red-oil broth 無渣紅油湯底, ranked among Chengdu's top hotpot brands). Entered Hong Kong May 2018 with a ~10,000 sq ft Mong Kok flagship; exited HK in 2024 after six years. No known US presence.

lmm.name: LMM
lmm.blurb: China-origin hand-smashed lemon-tea (手打檸檬茶, perfume-lemon 香水檸檬) chain with airport-themed stores (founder Guo Zhenye 郭震業); a 'river-crossing dragon' (過江龍) that entered Hong Kong in 2023. Exited HK in 2024. No known US presence. Distinct from Ningji 柠季, NingQi 柠気 and LINLEE 鄰里.

chajiu.name: Jo's Cha
chajiu.blurb: China-origin tea chain (Guangzhou) specializing in seasonal fruit- and vegetable-based teas. Entered Hong Kong and peaked at about 7 stores; has since downsized to ~5 amid the China F&B HK shakeout. No known US presence.

fufuland.name: fufuland
fufuland.blurb: China-origin fresh-milk soufflé (生乳舒芙蕾) dessert chain; a 'river-crossing dragon' that entered Hong Kong in 2024 with its sister brand 檸季 (Ningji) and peaked at ~11 HK stores before collapsing and fully exiting HK by July 2026. No known US presence. Origin company not firmly established.

laoxianghao.name: Lao Xiang Hao
laoxianghao.blurb: China-origin Hunan (湘) home-style stir-fry restaurant; a 'river-crossing dragon' (過江龍) that entered Hong Kong with a Mong Kok store but withdrew within months. China chain scale unconfirmed. No known US presence.

xishu.name: CHEZ CHOUX
xishu.blurb: China-origin cream-puff (泡芙) chain — founded in Shanghai (brand launched ~2010-2011; operated by Shanghai Moti Gongfang 上海摩提工房, est. 2003). Trades internationally as CHEZ CHOUX ('home of puffs'); ~400-700+ stores in China, with the parent group running 1,000+ stores across 150+ cities incl. Hong Kong. Present in HK with 10+ branches plus a new sub-line 'Puffin'. No known US presence.

luofen.name: Luo Fen Shi Jia
luofen.blurb: China-origin Jiangxi rice-noodle (江西米粉) brand from Nanchang; a 'river-crossing dragon' that entered Hong Kong with one Cheung Sha Wan store but withdrew after about a year. China chain scale unconfirmed. No known US presence. (HK operator billed as 花姐姐餐飲香港集團.)

meowbbq.name: Meow Barbecue
meowbbq.blurb: China-origin cat-themed barbecue (烤肉/燒肉) chain — founded 2012 by Fang Daqiang ('Uncle Meow'); combines Japanese-style meat selection, Korean-style marinade and Chinese cooking. 30+ stores across ~10 China cities (Beijing, Guangzhou, Shanghai, Chongqing); repeatedly ranked a Top-10 China BBQ brand. Overseas in Singapore (Bugis+ 2022, VivoCity 2024). Entered then exited Hong Kong. No known US presence.

baoshifu.name: Bao Shifu
baoshifu.blurb: China-origin bakery/pastry chain famous for its seaweed meat-floss cakes (海苔肉松小贝) — founded 2004 in Beijing by Bao Caisheng (鲍才胜); direct-operated (~100+ stores in China; well known for its anti-counterfeit trademark battles against copycats). Entering Hong Kong — first store site-selected at APM, Kwun Tong (not yet open). No known US presence.

tanyaxue.name: Tan Ya Xue
tanyaxue.blurb: China-origin Chengdu (Sichuan) duck-blood (鸭血) hotpot chain — launched 2018 (Chengdu-origin; founder Zhou Yang 周杨; celebrity-backed, co-founder comedian Liao Jian 廖健); franchise model. ~500 stores across 100+ China cities by 2020; the brand claimed ~1,000 globally by 2021 with overseas outlets in the US, Spain, Japan and Australia (unverified). China growth has since slowed.

_readme: Per-brand stock-listing intelligence for the Chains tab. For each brand: whether the brand OR a parent/controlling group is publicly listed, the exchange + exact ticker, the relationship, sister brands sharing the same portfolio, and whether its shares are China A-shares (SSE/SZSE/BSE) whose filings are rarely accessible to US investors. Tickers verified against exchange/IR/HKEXnews/SEC sources as of as_of; private = no verifiable listing. This is public-knowledge listing data, not the paywalled revenue analytics.

anta.note: Also RMB counter HKEX:82020; HSI constituent.

bestore.note: Hubei Bestore 良品铺子; Shanghai A-share, listed 24 Feb 2020.

cabbeen.note: 2018 privatization attempt did not complete; still trading.

chabaidao.note: Sichuan Baicha Baidao 四川百茶百道; IPO 23 Apr 2024 (HKEX:2555). SUSPENDED from trading 13 Oct 2026 by HKEX on an SFC order — the SFC suspects the IPO's share demand was manipulated and froze up to HK$4.379bn of 'Sun Ran Group' (孫然集團) assets (a record for such a case); shares were down ~77% from issue. Offline stores reportedly operate normally; investigation ongoing. Part of a broader SFC fraud case spanning three IPOs (also 撥康視雲 BoKang Shiyun and 天聚地合 Tianju Dihe): the SFC alleges IPO proceeds were diverted via non-public agreements into financial products and funneled back to major placees; ~HK$5bn frozen across the case; shares reportedly dropped from the Hang Seng Index; stock ~70%+ below issue (CTEE, 14 Oct 2026).

mixue.name: MIXUE
mixue.blurb: The largest food-and-beverage chain on earth by number of outlets — more units than McDonald's or Starbucks — built on ¥1 soft serve and cheap cheese-foam tea in China's smaller cities. Zhang Hongchao started it in 1997 with 3,000 yuan borrowed from his grandmother. Almost every store is a franchise, and the company earns less from drinks than from selling ingredients, equipment and packaging to its own franchisees, which is why it can open so many so fast. Its March 2025 Hong Kong listing was the year's most heavily subscribed.
mixue.why_watch: The only chain here that publishes its pipeline: US stores appear as 'coming soon' weeks before they trade, so its expansion is visible in advance rather than in hindsight.

chagee.name: CHAGEE
chagee.blurb: A premium 'modern teahouse' chain selling original-leaf tea with fresh milk, pitched at the space Starbucks occupies rather than at the bubble-tea price war. Zhang Junjie founded it in Yunnan in 2017 at twenty-three, after dropping out of school and working in a Taiwanese-style tea shop; the April 2025 Nasdaq IPO raised $411m and made him a billionaire. Its US stores are mall flagships — Century City, Brea, Del Amo — not street counters.
chagee.why_watch: The only chain in this archive that publishes coordinates for every US store, and the one making the most deliberate bet on American mall real estate.

luckin.name: Luckin Coffee
luckin.founder: Lu Zhengyao and Qian Zhiya (both since ousted)
luckin.listing: delisted from Nasdaq July 2020; OTC, with a US relisting reported as being prepared
luckin.blurb: China's biggest coffee chain, and bigger there than Starbucks. It is also the most notorious company in this group: after a 2019 Nasdaq IPO it admitted in April 2020 to fabricating more than $300m of sales, paid a $180m SEC penalty, was delisted, and went through Chapter 15. It then rebuilt under new management into a roughly 30,000-store, app-first operation (order on the phone, collect at a counter, little seating), and is reported to be preparing a return to a US listing.
luckin.why_watch: Because of the fraud, its own figures are worth checking against an independent count, which is what this project does. Its US stores publish no coordinates, so they are counted here by state but cannot be placed on the map.

popmart.name: POP MART
popmart.global_stores: 530+ stores worldwide at Dec 2024, plus roboshops
popmart.us_entry: East Rutherford, NJ (American Dream), September 2023 — first permanent store
popmart.blurb: Designer toys sold in blind boxes — you pay before you know which figure you get. Wang Ning founded it in 2010 as a Beijing variety store and turned it into an IP company: the Labubu character, designed by Kasing Lung, became a global craze that put Pop Mart bags on celebrities and queues outside its US malls. It is the one chain in scope selling objects rather than drinks.
popmart.why_watch: The clearest test of whether the Chinese chain wave in America is only tea and coffee. Its locator is behind bot management, so it is not collected here yet.

miniso.name: MINISO
miniso.listing: NYSE: MNSO (2020) and HKEX: 9896 (dual primary, July 2022)
miniso.global_stores: 8,485 worldwide at 31 Dec 2025 — 4,568 in China, 3,583 overseas
miniso.us_entry: Pasadena, California (88 W Colorado Blvd), April 2017
miniso.blurb: A cheap-and-cheerful variety chain — homeware, stationery, cosmetics, plush toys — that long presented itself with Japanese-styled branding despite being founded in Guangzhou in 2013. It has since leaned into licensed character goods (Disney, Sanrio, Barbie) and its own IP, and opened its 400th US store in August 2026, by far the largest American footprint of any chain in scope.
miniso.why_watch: The biggest prize and the biggest gap: roughly 400 US stores, and a locator this collector cannot read yet.

heytea.name: HEYTEA
heytea.blurb: The chain credited with inventing cheese-foam tea, which Nie Yunchen began selling from a small shop in Jiangmen in 2012 under the name Royal Tea. It built its reputation on design-led flagship stores and fruit teas at premium prices, and was the first of this wave to open in the United States, in New York at the end of 2023.
heytea.why_watch: The earliest mover of the current wave, which makes it the closest thing to a control case for how these US expansions mature.

cotti.name: Cotti Coffee
cotti.blurb: Founded in 2022 by the two executives forced out of Luckin over the accounting fraud, and set up in direct competition with it. Cotti competes with Luckin on price and has expanded very fast on a franchise model. Its US presence has grown quietly through individual franchisees near universities and in Chinese-American suburbs, rather than through a national rollout.
cotti.why_watch: A clear example of the price war that is pushing these chains abroad. It publishes no first-party US locator at all, which is part of why it cannot be counted here.

yangguofu.name: Yangguofu
yangguofu.global_stores: 6,000+ malatang outlets, overwhelmingly in China, as of 2025
yangguofu.us_entry: 2024, via franchisees (first US store unverified; franchisor entity established 8 April 2024)
yangguofu.blurb: One of China's two dominant malatang chains — build-your-own skewered hotpot soup, priced by weight. Founded in Harbin in 2003, it scaled to thousands of franchised outlets across China and began a registered US franchise programme in 2024, trading as YGF.
yangguofu.why_watch: The first chain this project found through a franchise filing rather than a storefront: its FDD lists every US outlet, which is how a chain with no online locator became countable. A test of whether malatang travels the way bubble tea and coffee have.

fishwithyou.name: Fish With You
fishwithyou.global_stores: several thousand sauerkraut-fish outlets in China (2025 est.)
fishwithyou.us_entry: Flushing, New York (135-25A 40th Rd); opening date unverified
fishwithyou.blurb: A Chinese fast-casual chain built on a single Sichuan dish — 酸菜鱼, sauerkraut (pickled mustard green) fish over rice. Founded in Beijing around 2016, it scaled to thousands of outlets across China on a low-price, single-format model and has begun franchising in the US, trading under its English name and the transliteration YONNY.
fishwithyou.why_watch: Found in the franchise-registry sweep, not on a storefront. A test of whether a single-dish Sichuan format travels the way bubble tea and coffee have — and, like Yangguofu, countable only through its filing, since its US web presence is one page per store.
